text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH

- President Demirel blocks the handover of the premiership to conservative leader Tansu Ciller under a power-sharing deal between the Islamists Welfare Party and the Ciller's True Path Party by giving the mandate to conservative Motherland Party leader Mesut Yilmaz.
- Cental Bank officails say no trouble forseen in the markets as Turkey enters an election period.
MILLIYET
- Prime Minister-designate Yilmaz says he would form a government in nine days.
- Leader of the Republican Peoples Party Deniz Baykal says all his MPs will back a Yilmaz government.
HURRIYET
- Ciller says Demirel's decision to give the mandate to Yilmaz was a "Presidential coup."
- Turkish troops kill 22 PKK militants and wound four others in southeastern Cudi mountain in a six-day security operation.
YENI YUZYIL
- Shareholders of an Islamist holding group Kombassan are in a panic after a court froze more than $100 milion worth of the firm's assets.
RADIKAL
- Yilmaz's government needs nine deputies to win a vote of confidence.
- Studies of the "build-operate" model for thermal power plant construction is complete, with a draft law awaiting parliament's approval.
CUMHURIYET
- Former Islamist-led coalition partners are angered by Demirel's decision to give the mandate to Yilmaz, bypassing their own formula for an "election" government.
DUNYA
- Pinar dairy products is the most active company on the Istanbul stock exchange.
ZAMAN
- Turkish Cypriot President Rauf Denktash says any agreement on the divided island of Cyprus depends on the Greek Cypriot community.
